text:
Nina: Heads-up — customer 'orbit' hit a spike and we returned a bunch of 413s on /v1/embeddings. seems like they started gzipping their JSON payloads. preflight only looks at Content-Length (post-compression) and our framing validator choked.
Marc: do we have the sample payload or logs? curious whether they changed shape or just compressed.
Nina: copied the failing curl and runtime reject: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \
  -d @vectors.json.gz
```
runtime: `ingress: preflight failed: declared_frames=0 compressed=true -> invalid_frame(413)`
Priya: we've historically rejected compressed bodies to keep unit accounting simple. decompressing at edge complicates quota (do we bill compressed bytes or expand to vector-units?).
Theo: product/billing note: our billing model is vector-units = sum(ceil(len/256)) across vectors. switching to bytes would be surprising. But we can accept compressed payload if client provides a deterministic hint header.
Marc: suggestion: add optional header `X-Embed-Compression: gzip; vectors=80;avg_len=512` so clients tell us original vector count/avg length. we validate header, then choose policy.
Priya: policy options: (A) reject until client sends uncompressed (strict); (B) decompress and bill by vector-units (accurate but costs CPU); (C) accept compressed and bill by bytes for tenants with burst-credit or negotiated contract.
Nina: Orbit is fine with option C if it avoids them re-uploading. they'd accept being billed by bytes with a visible note in console.
Theo: implementation implications: if we decompress at the edge we must ensure downstream workers see identical payloads — routing affinity matters because of KV cache locality for later calls. propose adding `X-Affinity-Key: tenant-orbit-session-xyz` to keep short-lived affinity.
Marc: also: telemetry. console should show: compressed_in_bytes, decompressed_bytes, reported_vectors, computed_vectors, billing_method. expose a chart for billed_unit_delta (post - pre).
Priya: for canary: opt-in beta flagged per-tenant. rollout plan: beta->5%->25%->100 over 3 weeks, monitor error-rate, billed-delta, edge-cpu-percent. console-bot: created canary card template.
ingest-bot: alert: tenant=orbit embed_reject_rate=9% window=10m threshold=2%
Nina: ok action list: 1) API: accept optional `X-Embed-Compression` and `X-Affinity-Key` headers (Marc), 2) runtime: add toggle to decompress-on-ingress and per-tenant policy (Priya), 3) billing: define bytes->vector-units fallback and rounding rules (Theo), 4) console: new telemetry and a billed-delta diff card for beta tenants (Nina).
Marc: I'll open an RFC with header parsing rules and validation (examples + failure modes).
Theo: I'll draft the billing mapping: if header present, prefer reported_vectors; else if decompress enabled compute vectors and bill normally; else bill by bytes with conversion = ceil(bytes/1024) as temporary metric (we should debate the constant).
Priya: prefer using reported_vectors when header signed by client key? trust issue. maybe require the header be signed with tenant's API key HMAC to avoid fraud.
Nina: good call — add `X-Embed-Meta-Sig` option in RFC for trusted clients.
Marc: small UX detail: if we accept compressed-bytes billing show a tooltip: "This request billed by compressed bytes due to tenant policy; uncompressed unit estimate: X".
console-bot: created dashboard draft at /console/drafts/compression-canary-1745560000
Nina: let's start with opt-in beta for partners and iterate. I'll coordinate with Orbit product contact and draft messaging about billing transparency.
Theo: tagging billing/product for review of conversion constant. piya@billing, can you weigh in?
Priya: will follow up. short-term: reject by default, opt-in for beta.
Nina: thanks all — filing tickets and setting canary gate. :thumbsup:
